comments.text: A factoid from the BTS features you missed: Christopher Lee was an intelligence officer in WWII and had some pretty...specific...combat training and experience. So when Peter Jackson asked him to scream as Grima stabbed him, he said that's not what being stabbed in the back would do to a person. Being stabbed would drive all the air OUT of a person's lungs, so instead of gasping inward or being able to force air through the vocal chords, a person would be forced to exhale with no control, and it would be much quieter than the scream PJ was hoping for. PJ was very concerned about how Sir Lee knew that, but wisely opted not to ask further.

comments.text: 17:07 Density isn't the only issue here. Lava reacts violently with water, immediately turning it into superheated steam. Since humans are mostly water, his body would actually begin to break apart in the lava as the water content turned to steam. This would trigger a small mini-eruption of lava as the moisture created steam, and those bubbles would lower the density of lava at the surface, causing him to sink. There is a video online of a guy throwing a bag of meat into a volcano, and that is exactly what happens, but we don't see that mechanism depicted in the movie.

comments.text: 14:41 "In this scene, during the filming with the Old White Wizard and Christopher, the director, Peter Jackson, wanted him to scream as he got stabbed in the back. However, Christopher Lee told the director: 'I saw a world war and fought hand-to-hand on the front lines. A person who is stabbed in the back—especially if the knife punctures the lungs—cannot scream. Because the lungs collapse instantly, they can only make a muffled, gasping sound, like a groan. They cannot scream because the lungs cannot inflate to produce that sound.' After giving this detailed explanation, the director accepted it."
